info.name: Jibble API
info.description:
API Introduction

The Jibble API follows the REST architecture. The URLs have a predictable structure that is resource based, accepts JSON-encoded request bodies and returns JSON-encoded responses. It also uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication and verbs.

Some requests can also be used with filters.

It is possible to test the API on the test environment without affecting your live data.

OData Query Options

Jibble's API supports query options to customize the information retrieved. For more details refer to Query Options documentation.

Errors

Jibble uses standard HTTP response codes to indicate success or failure of a request. In case of an error, the response body should contain more details on the problem.

Async requests for OData collection endpoints

This guide explains how to use asynchronous API requests.
It is intended for API consumers who need to export or fetch large OData collections without keeping a long-running HTTP connection open.

What this feature does

For supported collection GET endpoints, add:

Prefer: respond-async

When this header is present, the API accepts the request and returns a job reference instead of the full dataset immediately.
You then poll the export status and download the result when ready.

Supported request shape

  • Method: GET

  • Endpoint type: OData collection endpoint (for example: /v1/People)

  • Optional OData options: $filter, $orderby, $select, $expand (and combinations)

  • Header: Prefer: respond-async

If Prefer: respond-async is not sent, the endpoint behaves normally and returns a synchronous response.

Endpoints that do not support async mode

Not every endpoint supports async exports.
For non-async endpoints (Timesheets endpoints, for example), sending Prefer: respond-async does not return an async export job and the endpoint behaves as a normal synchronous API call.

Use this quick check:

  • Async-capable endpoint: returns 202 Accepted with exportId and statusUrl.

  • Non-async endpoint: returns its regular response shape (usually 200 OK) without exportId/statusUrl.

Step 1: Start an async request

Example

GET <service-host>/v1/People?$select=id,fullName,status&$expand=organization&$filter=contains(fullName,'Export')&$orderby=fullName
Authorization: Bearer {{person_access_token}}
Prefer: respond-async

Response

  • Status: 202 Accepted

  • Headers:

    • Preference-Applied: respond-async

    • Location: /v1/AsyncExports({exportId})

  • Body:

{
  "exportId": "d7d6d82a-ae1b-4dda-b47a-4d8fce95be58",
  "status": "Pending",
  "statusUrl": "/v1/AsyncExports(d7d6d82a-ae1b-4dda-b47a-4d8fce95be58)"
}

Note: for duplicate requests, the API may return an existing export ID instead of creating a new one.
statusUrl is a relative URL; call it on the same service host that received the original request.

Deduplication and getting a fresh export

Async export creation uses deduplication per user.

  • Two requests are considered duplicates when they target the same entity and use the same raw query string (same parameters).

  • If a duplicate is found, the API returns the existing export instead of creating a new one.

  • This means repeated calls can return the same exportId until that export is removed or expires.

To force a fresh export with the same parameters:

  1. Delete the existing export: DELETE /v1/AsyncExports({exportId}), or

  2. Wait until the existing export expires based on retention.

Step 2: Poll export status

Use the statusUrl (or Location) from step 1:

GET <service-host>/v1/AsyncExports({{export_id}})
Authorization: Bearer {{person_access_token}}

Possible status response:

{
  "exportId": "d7d6d82a-ae1b-4dd2-b47a-4d8fce95be58",
  "status": "Processing",
  "entityType": "Jibble.TimeTracking.Model.Person",
  "createdAt": "2026-02-26T13:20:10.2877721+00:00",
  "lastUpdatedAt": "2026-02-26T13:20:11.1142432+00:00",
  "responseSizeBytes": null,
  "error": null
}

Status values:

  • Pending

  • Processing

  • Completed

  • Failed

If status is Failed, check the error field.

Step 3: Download completed result

When an export is completed, polling endpoint returns:

  • Status: 303 See Other

  • Header: Location:

Many HTTP clients automatically follow redirects; in that case you usually receive 200 OK from S3 with the exported JSON.

The exported payload is OData JSON:

{
  "@odata.context": "https://<service-host>/$metadata#Collection(Person)",
  "@odata.count": 3,
  "value": [
    {
      "id": "....",
      "fullName": "Export Alpha",
      "organization": { "id": "....", "name": "..." }
    }
  ]
}

Additional export management endpoints

List your exports

GET <service-host>/v1/AsyncExports
Authorization: Bearer {{person_access_token}}

Returns an array of your export records.

Delete an export

DELETE <service-host>/v1/AsyncExports({{export_id}})
Authorization: Bearer {{person_access_token}}

Returns 204 No Content.

Retention and URL expiration

  • Export state is retained for a limited time (default is 24 hours, deployment-configurable).

  • Download URLs are pre-signed and expire (default is 24 hours, deployment-configurable).

  • If an export has expired, polling may return 404 Not Found.

Error handling and limits

  • 429 Too Many Requests: too many active exports for the user.
    Example body:

      {
    "error": "Too many concurrent exports",
    "maxConcurrentExports": 5
  }

  • 404 Not Found: export does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated user.

  • 200 OK + status: "Failed": export failed asynchronously; inspect error.

End-to-end cURL example

# 1) Start async request
curl -i --request GET \
  --url "https://time-tracking.prod.jibble.io/v1/People?\$select=id,fullName&\$expand=organization" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  --header "Prefer: respond-async"
# 2) Poll status (repeat until completed or failed)
curl -i --request GET \
  --url "https://time-tracking.prod.jibble.io/v1/AsyncExports(<exportId>)" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Best practices for API clients

  • Poll with a small delay (for example 1-3 seconds) and apply backoff for longer-running exports.

  • Handle both 303 redirects and auto-followed 200 responses from S3.

  • Treat Failed as terminal and surface error to logs/telemetry.

  • Delete exports you no longer need.

request.description:
Create a Schedule Object.

Request Body

  • name (string): Required. Display name of the schedule

  • workArrangement (string, enum): Possible values: Fixed, Flexible. If Fixed value is set, then in daySchedule array items required to have fields from and to. If Flexible, then duration is reqiured for items in daySchedule

  • daySchedules (array): Settings for particular day

    • day (string): Day of the week

    • from (string, HH:MM:SS format): Time of the day from which fixed day should start

    • to (string, HH:MM:SS format): Time of the end of the fixed day

    • duration (string, ISO 8601) : Duration of the flexible day

  • breaksType (string, enum): Possiblevalues: Paid, Unpaid. Only one type of break per schedule.

  • breaks (array): Collection of breaks

    • id (uuid): Required. Unique Id of the break.

    • name (string): Display name of the break.

    • duration (string, ISO 8601): Duration of the break.

    • allowToBeTakenFromTo (bool): Optional. Flag indicating if break can be anytime or during particular time of the day (see from and to fields below).

    • from (string, HH:MM:SS format): Optional. Time of the day since when break can be taken.

    • to (string, HH:MM:SS format): Optional. Time of the day until when break can be taken.

API Endpoint: Get Screenshots

This endpoint retrieves a list of screenshots associated with a specific date and person. The results can be filtered, ordered, and expanded to include additional information about the person associated with each screenshot.

Request Parameters

  • $expand: Expands the person object to include specific fields. In this case, it retrieves the fullName of the person.

  • $filter: Filters the results based on two criteria:

    • belongsToDate: The date associated with the screenshots (e.g., 2026-04-23).

    • person/id: The unique identifier for the person (e.g., 12338863-4f52-4873-a022-3004d7b7c677).

  • $orderby: Specifies the order of the results based on the time field in ascending order.

  • $select: Specifies the fields to include in the response, such as url, id, time, and status.

Response Structure

The response will be a JSON object containing the following structure:

  • value: An array of screenshot objects, each containing:

    • time: The timestamp of when the screenshot was taken.

    • url: The link to access the screenshot.

    • status: The current status of the screenshot.

    • id: The unique identifier for the screenshot.

    • person: An object containing:

      • fullName: The full name of the person associated with the screenshot.

    Displayed name of the pay period definition.

  • startAtDayNumberSecond (integer):
